title: Microsoft Purview: Priority cleanup to permanently delete Exchange mailbox items under holds (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing requirements, tenant switch, policy creation command and audit controls are supported. Two minor corrections remain: cite the documentation establishing that review-set data requires case deletion, and remove the checklist instruction for a Relabel control that has no corresponding controls-table row.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup is a Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management feature for permanently deleting sensitive Exchange mailbox content.
claims.quote: Use the Priority cleanup feature under Data Lifecycle Management in Microsoft Purview when you need to permanently delete sensitive content from Exchange mailboxes

claims.claim: Priority cleanup can delete items despite retention settings that would retain them.
claims.quote: despite retention settings that retain the item or eDiscovery holds.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup can override eDiscovery holds.
claims.quote: Although priority cleanup can override eDiscovery holds

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a recurring exception to delete Exchange items under a broader retention policy or legal hold.
claims.quote: The first release of Priority cleanup enables admins to create a recurring exception to delete items under a broader retention policy and/or legal hold on Exchange workload.

claims.claim: The roadmap says creating a priority cleanup requires a separate security role.
claims.quote: Creating a Priority cleanup will require a separate security role

claims.claim: The roadmap says creating a priority cleanup requires multiple approvers.
claims.quote: Creating a Priority cleanup will require a separate security role, multiple approvers

claims.claim: The roadmap promises a complete audit trail.
claims.quote: and will have a complete audit trail.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes the feature as rolling out in preview and subject to change.
claims.quote: Priority cleanup is rolling out in preview and subject to change.

claims.claim: A priority cleanup policy can use adaptive or static scope.
claims.quote: For Choose the type of priority cleanup, select Adaptive or Static then select Next.

claims.claim: Policy creation uses a KeyQL query to identify content.
claims.quote: For the Tell us what you're looking for page, enter text into the KeyQL editor box to construct a query using Exchange email properties.

claims.claim: A policy can delete matched items as soon as possible or retain them for a specified period before deletion.
claims.quote: choose whether to permanently delete the matched items as soon as possible or retain them for a specific period and then delete them.

claims.claim: The policy creator specifies approvers during policy configuration.
claims.quote: For the Assign who'll approve what gets deleted page, this is where you need to specify another priority cleanup approver

claims.claim: Items still follow the same deletion process and timings.
claims.quote: Items still go through the same deletion process with the same timings to ensure a compliant permanent deletion

claims.claim: Priority cleanup does not require waiting for a retention period to expire or a hold to be released.
claims.quote: there's no need to wait for the retention period to expire or the hold to be released.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: After the required approvals, permanently deleted items cannot be restored by users, administrators or Microsoft.
claims.quote: When all the required approvals are complete, items are permanently deleted and cannot be restored by users, by admins, or by Microsoft.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Exchange priority cleanup can override Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: Because the deletion is irreversible and can override existing holds and even Preservation Lock

claims.claim: Items marked as a record or regulatory record are excluded from actual priority cleanup.
claims.quote: You can't use priority cleanup for items that are marked as a record or regulatory record.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot delete data already copied into an eDiscovery review set.
claims.quote: the data might already be copied to an eDiscovery review set where it can't be deleted by priority cleanup.

claims.claim: Review-set data is deleted only when the eDiscovery case is deleted.
claims.quote: You can't delete items from a review set, and you can't delete review sets from a case. To delete a review set and its data, you must delete the eDiscovery case that contains the review set.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-review-set-manage to sources for the statement that review-set data is deleted only by deleting its case.

claims.claim: A mailbox must contain at least 10 MB of data to support priority cleanup.
claims.quote: A mailbox must have at least 10-MB data to support priority cleanup.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup also covers SharePoint and OneDrive, with different configuration and behavior.
claims.quote: Although you can use the priority cleanup feature for mailboxes and for files in SharePoint and OneDrive, the typical use cases are different. There are some other differences in behavior and configuration

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The tenant-level capability is enabled by default, so defaultState is on.
claims.quote: Because of the built-in safeguards, the feature itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.

claims.quote: This role is automatically added to the Organization Management role group but must be manually added to any other role group.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft suggests that highly regulated organizations using Preservation Lock consider disabling priority cleanup at tenant level.
claims.quote: highly regulated organizations that use Preservation Lock might want the additional safeguard of turning off priority cleanup at the tenant level

claims.claim: Priority cleanup deletion requires a policy and its required approvals; enabling the capability alone does not delete mailbox content.
claims.quote: When the priority cleanup policy is turned on and items are identified, approvers for the policy are notified by email. When all the required approvals are complete, items are permanently deleted and cannot be restored by users, by admins, or by Microsoft.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Simulation is recommended but not required for Exchange priority cleanup.
claims.quote: | Simulation required before running the policy: | No (but recommended) | Yes |

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The first-stage priority cleanup approver should differ from the creator, but that separation is not enforced.
claims.quote: This should be a different person to the user who created the priority cleanup policy, but isn't enforced.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Approvers must be individual users.
claims.quote: Approvers must be individual users.

claims.claim: Mail-enabled security groups are not currently supported as approvers.
claims.quote: Mail-enabled security groups are not currently supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Scope; controls[1].note
claims.claim: Approvers need the documented stage-specific roles assigned before policy creation.
claims.quote: The approver at each stage of the review process must have the correct roles assigned before the policy can be created.

claims.claim: Policy creation fails with an error if a reviewer lacks the required roles.
claims.quote: If the reviewer at any stage doesn't have the correct roles assigned in advance, policy creation fails with an error.

claims.claim: After required approvals, deletion proceeds without a further action, and Microsoft says to allow up to seven days.
claims.quote: When all the required approvals are complete, items are permanently deleted and cannot be restored by users, by admins, or by Microsoft. Allow up to seven days for items to be permanently deleted.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: An approver who rejects permanent deletion must relabel the item using an existing retention label.
claims.quote: If an approver doesn't agree to permanently delete an identified item, they must assign an existing retention label (any configuration) to the item.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Items might still be permanently deleted after a policy is deleted if its approval process was already complete.
claims.quote: Although you can delete a priority cleanup policy, if the approval process for it is complete, items might still be permanently deleted.

claims.quote: The name is visible to end users, but the optional description is visible only to priority cleanup admins and the policy's specified approvers.

claims.claim: After final approval, the item silently disappears from Outlook.
claims.quote: After the final priority cleanup approval, the item silently disappears from Outlook.

claims.claim: The two mailbox-specific audit operations currently lack friendly names in the Purview portal.

claims.claim: The Exchange feature page's prerequisites discuss permissions and approvers, without naming a licence.
claims.quote: Searched: 'priority cleanup Exchange pricing meter add-on price Purview'; opened priority-cleanup-exchange, including Prerequisites, Permissions, Policy approvers and Enable auditing; no licence named in those prerequisites.

claims.claim: No separate Priority cleanup meter is listed on the cited feature and licensing pages.
claims.quote: Searched: 'priority cleanup Exchange pricing meter add-on price Purview'; opened priority-cleanup-exchange and microsoft-purview-service-description; searched the service description for price, meter, $, and add-on. No Priority cleanup meter found.

claims.claim: Any user benefiting from the service requires a licence.
claims.quote: Any user benefiting from the service requires a license.

claims.claim: Users assigned a Purview role for the portal count as benefiting users who need a licence.
claims.quote: Users with a Purview role assigned for use in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Users associated with Exchange user mailboxes require the relevant licence when a Purview feature is used there.
claims.quote: Exchange user mailboxes, OneDrive accounts, Teams chats, and devices are associated with a user account, so the user must have the required license assigned when a Purview policy or feature is used in these locations.

claims.claim: The cited feature and service-description pages do not publish an add-on price.
claims.quote: Searched: 'priority cleanup Exchange pricing meter add-on price Purview'; opened priority-cleanup-exchange and microsoft-purview-service-description and searched the latter for price, meter, $ and add-on. Neither page supplies an add-on price.

claims.claim: Approvers review cleanup items on Pending cleanups.
claims.quote: They can select the link in the notification and reminder emails to go directly to the Data lifecycle management > Priority cleanup > Pending cleanups page in the portal to review the content to approve.

claims.claim: The Priority Cleanup Admin role is required to create and manage priority cleanup policies.
claims.quote: This role is required to create and manage priority cleanup policies

claims.claim: Enabling or disabling the feature requires the Priority Cleanup Admin role.
claims.quote: This role is required to create and manage priority cleanup policies, enable or disable the feature

claims.claim: Approving items in the initial stage requires the Priority Cleanup Admin role.
claims.quote: This role is required to create and manage priority cleanup policies, enable or disable the feature, or approve items within the initial approval stage.

claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Viewer permits viewing policies and settings without making changes.
claims.quote: the Priority Cleanup Viewer role allows only the visibility of priority cleanup policies and settings without the ability to make changes or create new policies.

claims.claim: Content Explorer List Viewer and Content Explorer Content Viewer are required to view content in simulation and approval stages.

claims.claim: Group mailboxes are supported only through adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: Group mailboxes are supported via adaptive scopes only.

claims.claim: A single cleanup policy cannot combine Exchange with SharePoint and OneDrive locations.
claims.quote: you can't create a cleanup policy for all three locations in same policy.

claims.claim: Adaptive scopes must exist before an adaptive priority cleanup policy is created.
claims.quote: If you decide to use an adaptive policy, you must create one or more adaptive scopes before you create your priority cleanup policy

claims.claim: Auditing must be enabled at least one day before the first policy is created and run.
claims.quote: Make sure that auditing is enabled at least one day before you create and run the first priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: The tenant-level priority cleanup switch also affects SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: When you turn off priority cleanup, you're turning it off for SharePoint and OneDrive as well as for Exchange.

claims.claim: Turning off the tenant control blocks new policies but existing policies continue functioning.
claims.quote: New priority cleanup policies can't be created until you turn on the control and select Save again. If priority cleanup policies are already created when you turn off the control: Existing priority cleanup policies continue to function

claims.claim: Existing policies can be deleted while the tenant switch is off.
claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can be deleted

claims.claim: Existing policies cannot be modified while the tenant switch is off.
claims.quote: Existing priority cleanup policies can't be modified

claims.claim: Learn directs readers to Purview permissions guidance for assigning the required roles or creating role groups.
claims.quote: For instructions to add users to the default roles or create your own role groups, use the following guidance: Permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal

claims.claim: The tenant switch is in Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration > control for priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management. From the top right, select Priority cleanup settings. From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup, and select Save.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not document an automation route for the tenant-level on/off switch at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'priority cleanup tenant disable enable PowerShell Set-PolicyConfig PriorityCleanup' and '"priority cleanup" "tenant" "PowerShell" disable'; read tenant-switch instructions and searched Set-PolicyConfig reference for Priority/Cleanup; no automation documented.

claims.claim: Policy creation starts in Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup, and then select + Create a priority cleanup.

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -PriorityCleanup creates a priority cleanup policy in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. The PriorityCleanup switch specifies whether to create a Priority cleanup policy. You don't need to specify a value with this switch.

claims.claim: Audit searches are available in Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select the Audit solution card. On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <date> -EndDate <date> -Operations PriorityCleanupDelete searches that documented operation in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Search-UnifiedAuditLog
    -EndDate <ExDateTime>
    -StartDate <ExDateTime>
    [-Operations <String[]>]
The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation.

claims.claim: A policy's cleanup ID can be used as an audit keyword search term.
claims.quote: Use the details of a policy to identify its cleanup ID, and paste this number as a keyword search string from the auditing solution.

claims.claim: Policy status is monitored on the Priority cleanup page.
claims.quote: You can monitor the status of priority cleanups for each policy from Data lifecycle management > Priority cleanup.

claims.claim: Learn's policy-approver section states that three approvals are always required.
claims.quote: Three approvals are always required, irrespective of which type of hold is applied to the item

claims.claim: Learn's approval-process section instead describes retention and eDiscovery approval stages conditionally.
claims.quote: Then if the items have retention settings applied, they require a next stage approval from retention admins. And finally, if the items are included in an eDiscovery hold, they also require another approval from an eDiscovery admin.

claims.claim: Learn characterizes typical Exchange priority-cleanup policy use as rare.
claims.quote: | Typical policy use: | Rare | For Teams meeting recordings and transcripts: Continual

claims.claim: The mixed entitlement model reflects coverage through qualifying Microsoft 365 or Office 365 plans and Purview-related suites.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5; Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW; Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW; Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance; Office 365 E5/A5/G5

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Microsoft Purview as the product.
claims.quote: "products": [ "Microsoft Purview" ]
